summary: Jens Peter Laut specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. In 2008, he succeeded Klaus Röhrborn, holding posts at the University of Göttingen (circa 2008-2021) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (circa 2008).

Jens Schlieter works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Bonn, completing his PhD under Josef Simon. He became a professor at the University of Bern around 2008.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earning degrees at Munich and Göttingen. He held professorships at Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin (1995-2001), and served as professor at the University of Munich (1999-2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim studied under teacher Rosemary Smith and completed a PhD at SOAS University of London by 2011 under the supervision of Youngsook Pak.

Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of Sinology and art history who studied at Stanford and the University of Oregon. He held major posts at the University of Washington (circa 1975-2001) and Princeton University (circa 2001-2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań. He served there as head of General and Comparative Linguistics in 1969 and as professor from 1977 to 1991.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and under Antoine Meillet. He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (circa 1926-1946) and Jagiellonian University (circa 1946-1965).

Jessie Pons is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University by 2011 and was Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.
Ji Hao is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota under the supervision of Paul Rouzer. In 2017, Hao held an attested post at the College of the Holy Cross.

Ji Zhe specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing a PhD in sociology at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences by 2007. He served as Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011-2017).
Jian Deng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a disciple under Weijue Shi, whom Deng succeeded in 2005.

Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Yang Wenhui from circa 1904 to 1911. He founded the China Inner Studies College and served as its head from circa 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Nankai University and Harvard University, supervised by Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello. Wu served as a professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011-2018).
Jianming Hu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hu studied at Waseda University and held a researcher post at Komazawa University, both attested in 2015.
Jiaqi Wang was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Wang studied under Gangkar Rinpoche and was a PhD student at Columbia University.

Jiayao An is an archaeologist and Sinologist who studied under Bai Su between circa 1978 and 1982. Around 1982, An was appointed a special researcher and Xi'an research office director at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Jiegang Gu was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Peking University under Zhang Taiyan and Hu Shih. He held posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. Abe completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973) and served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Lan studied at Tunghai University from circa 1965 to 1969 and served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from circa 1986 until retiring in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.
